title: What If the Population Doubled? (Short)

portraits.ethan: Photorealistic head-and-shoulders portrait of a man in his early 30s, short dark-blond hair, light stubble, blue-grey eyes, a small scar through his left eyebrow, navy work jacket, friendly tired expression, plain soft grey background, soft window light, sharp focus, 85mm lens.

looks.ethan: Ethan: early 30s man, short dark-blond hair, light stubble, blue-grey eyes, a small scar through his left eyebrow, wearing a navy work jacket, same face as the reference portrait

style: Cinematic photorealistic film still, vertical 9:16 composition with the subject centered, shallow depth of field, natural cinematic color grade, present-day setting, no text other than what is described.

scenes.image: Ethan opening his apartment door at dawn in a T-shirt, the hallway behind it packed with confused strangers in pajamas, vertical close-up.
lines: [intrigued] You wake up... and there are sixteen billion people on Earth.
scenes.motion: Ethan opens the door and freezes as the crowd of strangers turns toward him, handheld.

scenes.image: A Chicago street at sunrise jammed with thousands of bewildered people, vertical aerial view.
A supermarket with completely empty shelves and a crowd pushing carts.
lines: [urgent] By lunch, the supermarkets are empty.

scenes.image: A dinner plate cut neatly in half with a knife, one half empty, overhead light.
lines: The world grows enough food for everyone... once. Split it in half, and nobody gets enough.

scenes.image: A city skyline at night with neighborhoods going dark in rolling blackouts.
lines: Week one. The power grid can't keep up. Blackouts roll from city to city.

scenes.image: A football stadium turned into a giant shelter, rows of cots across the field.
lines: Every stadium becomes a shelter. And it's still not enough.

scenes.image: Ethan's tiny apartment crowded with a family of strangers sleeping on the floor, Ethan stepping over them holding coffee.
lines: [wry] My one-bedroom has six people in it now.

scenes.image: A massive line of job seekers wrapped around a city block.
lines: [serious] Billions need jobs. Wages crash. Rents explode.

scenes.image: A young woman teaching kids on a whiteboard in a tent-city classroom.
lines: [hopeful] But twice the people also means twice the doctors... twice the inventors... twice the chance of the next Einstein.

scenes.image: Earth at night from space with city lights twice as dense and bright.
An impossibly crowded crosswalk seen from above, hundreds crossing in every direction.
lines: Would you want to live in a world with twice as many people?
